I'm working on VictoriaMetrics and noticed that the Graphite tag series registration endpoints are currently creating new time series as a side effect when called.

*   The HTTP endpoint for registering a single Graphite tag series (POST to /graphite/tags/tagSeries in single-node mode, and POST to /select/<tenant>/graphite/tags/tagSeries in cluster mode) must return HTTP 501 Not Implemented.

*   The HTTP endpoint for registering multiple Graphite tag series (POST to /graphite/tags/tagMultiSeries in single-node mode, and POST to /select/<tenant>/graphite/tags/tagMultiSeries in cluster mode) must return HTTP 501 Not Implemented.

*   When the tagSeries endpoint is called, no new time series must be created as a side effect.

*   When the tagMultiSeries endpoint is called with multiple records, no new time series must be created as a side effect.

*   The GraphiteTagsTagSeries method on both Vmselect and Vmsingle test helper types must have no return value and must validate that the server returns HTTP 501 Not Implemented.

All changes compile cleanly with no other non-test callers. Here's a summary of what I implemented:

**`app/vmselect/main.go`** (covers both single-node and cluster mode, since single-node embeds vmselect's `RequestHandler`):
- `/tags/tagSeries` case now returns HTTP 501 Not Implemented via `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotImplemented)` instead of delegating to `graphite.TagsTagSeriesHandler`. The request counter still increments, but the Graphite handler is never called, so no time series are created.
- `/tags/tagMultiSeries` case does the same.

**`apptest/model.go`**:
- `PrometheusQuerier.GraphiteTagsTagSeries` and `GraphiteTagsTagMultiSeries` now declared with no return value.

**`apptest/vmselect.go`** and **`apptest/vmsingle.go`**:
- Both `GraphiteTagsTagSeries` and `GraphiteTagsTagMultiSeries` helpers now return nothing and assert the server responds with `http.StatusNotImplemented` (501) rather than 200/parsing a body.

The `graphite.TagsTagSeriesHandler`/`TagsTagMultiSeriesHandler` functions remain in the graphite package (exported, so no unused-symbol issue) but are no longer wired into the router.
